title: Money you may already be owed

scenes.head: Money you may already be owed
scenes.line: Eh, have a seat and let's have our money talk, quickly. You may have dividends sitting somewhere with your name on them, and you don't even know it.
scenes.img: A Nigerian woman in her fifties at a kitchen table in Lagos, looking surprised and happy at old share certificates and letters, warm evening light

scenes.head: Why dividends go missing
scenes.body: No e-dividend mandate, an old address or bank account, or your name spelt differently
scenes.line: So, how does a dividend go missing? Most times, there is no e-dividend mandate, the address or bank account is old, or your name is spelt differently in different places.
scenes.img: A pile of old unopened envelopes and faded paper cheques on a wooden desk, dusty, nostalgic mood, Nigerian setting

scenes.head: Step 1: Find the registrar
scenes.body: Every listed company has one. The name is in its annual report.
scenes.line: Step one. Find the company's registrar. Every listed company has one, and you will find the name in its annual report or on its website. The registrar keeps the list of shareholders.
scenes.img: A young Nigerian man reading a company annual report booklet at a desk with a laptop, focused, modern Lagos office

scenes.head: Step 2: Ask, with your details
scenes.body: Full name, old addresses, CSCS number and BVN
scenes.line: Step two. Contact the registrar with your full name, any old address you used, your Central Securities Clearing System number if you have one, and your Bank Verification Number. Ask them to check for unclaimed dividends.
scenes.img: A Nigerian man on a phone call holding a notepad with a checklist, calm and organised, bright office

scenes.head: Step 3: Fill the e-dividend mandate
scenes.body: Future dividends go straight into your bank account
scenes.line: Step three. Complete the e-dividend mandate form through your broker or the registrar. Once that is done, future dividends go straight into your bank account. No more lost cheques.
scenes.img: A smiling Nigerian woman looking at a banking app notification on her smartphone showing money received, close-up, warm light

scenes.head: Know the stock before you buy the story.

scenes.line: If you inherited shares from family, check those too. One simple money lesson every weekday on moloneystreetre.com. Know the stock before you buy the story. See you on Moloney Street.
